question: LOKI_SIMPLE=1 cuts the assembled prompt 78%. That is a TOKEN measurement. Does the stripped arm still build the thing, and does it take more or fewer iterations?
method: benchmarks/run-prompt-ablation.sh, 3 trials per arm. ONE engine copy, same spec, model (sonnet), caps and machine -- the arms differ by a single environment variable read at prompt-assembly time. The engine stamps prompt_arm from its OWN environment and the harness refuses to record a trial where that disagrees with the harness label, so arm attribution cannot silently drift. Acceptance is an artifact check (greet.js_exists), not a self-report.

result.acceptance: 3/3 in BOTH arms -- no regression from stripping the prompt
result.act_iterations: 1 in every run of both arms -- no change

verdict: NO OUTCOME REGRESSION MEASURED, and NO SPEED CLAIM AVAILABLE. Wall clock is completely separated -- every simple run beat every full run -- but at 3 trials per arm the smallest achievable two-sided p is 0.1, so even perfect separation cannot clear alpha. Reported UNDERPOWERED rather than as an 18% win.
why_underpowered_not_a_win: With n=3 vs n=3 there are only 20 possible splits, so the exact permutation floor is 2/20 = 0.1. n=4 per arm would drop the floor to 0.0286 and n=5 to 0.0079. The separation is real; the DESIGN cannot certify it. Publishing '18% faster' from this would be a typed multiplier.
not_claimed: No multiplier is reported. The 78% prompt reduction is a TOKEN measurement and says nothing about outcomes; only the acceptance and iteration results below speak to behaviour. Arms differ by one environment variable in one binary on one machine -- nothing here compares Loki to another vendor.
